AI NEWS DAILY — 12 Nov 2026

TOP STORY
Anthropic opened its IPO roadshow at $70-78 a share: 825M Class A shares on Nasdaq as ANT, about $1.4T fully diluted at the top of the range, up to ~$64B raised, pricing expected Nov 18. The filing also carries a $26B private placement of non-voting stock at the IPO price to AMD, Broadcom, Google, Micron, Microsoft, Nvidia and TSMC.

5 KEY UPDATES
1. Google made Gemini 4 Carbon generally available at $2/$10 per million tokens until Nov 30, then $4/$20, and shipped Gemini Decision 1 with a Decisions API that bills zero output tokens ($0.10 per 1M input, up to 1,000 closed-ended questions per call).
2. Meituan released LongCat-2.5, a 1.6T-parameter MoE with ~48B active, under the MIT licence on Hugging Face. Moonshot shipped Kimi K3.1 Pro (2.8T total, 104B active, 1M context) and Baidu put out ERNIE 5.5 Flash Preview with Apache 2.0 weights promised.
3. DeepMind's AlphaProof Code agents wrote 6M+ lines of Lean proofs verifying security properties of the compiled code behind Signal's protocol in about four weeks, catching two deliberately reintroduced bugs. Verification artefacts will be open-sourced.
4. AlphaGenome 2 predicts DNA variant effects per cell type (107M cell profiles, 30% of causal variants on TenK10K vs 16% before), and Gemini Robotics 2.5 posted a 96% success rate on live Mercedes-Benz production lines in Hungary and Germany.
5. Safety ledger: Fireworks AI widened its October breach to include billing data and partial model weights; New York opened RAISE Act registration (Jan 1, 2027 deadline, 72-hour incident reporting, up to $3M penalties); Australia will consider a criminal offence for AI companies over harmful model conduct.

CONCEPT OF THE DAY — The decision tier
The cheapest AI work is no longer writing. Routing, tool selection, relevance checks and rubric scoring are closed-set judgments, and Google now prices them at input tokens only while Meta's Muse Ember does the same job at ten cents per million. Generating a token needs a forward pass per token; classifying does not, which is why a decision endpoint can quote 150-250ms latency. The catch is calibration: a confidence score is only useful if 0.9 really means ninety percent, so measure it on your own traffic.
